subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw enforce before externally or plugin-registered recurring `agentTurn` cron jobs can run with inherited model and spend exposure?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, model-provider spend policy, persisted doctor/update behavior, and quota thresholds, so automation cannot safely choose the boundary.

options.title: Approve coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin `agentTurn` jobs, make inherited model-cost exposure explicit, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Ship a narrow model-cost guard
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block when a recurring `agentTurn` job inherits a high-cost default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split into existing RFCs
options.body: Resolve provenance, reason-aware backoff, budget enforcement, and schema gaps separately while accepting that consent and model-inheritance policy remains fragmented for now.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin `agentTurn` jobs, make inherited model-cost exposure explicit, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron scheduling, plugin scheduled turns, and model-selection surfaces, and the decision spans those boundaries.
